key_insight: The HOPE trial tests whether a shorter, dose-painted pelvic radiotherapy schedule can reduce acute gastrointestinal toxicity while maintaining cancer control in stage I–IIB cervical cancer.
clinical_relevance: If successful, this approach could make concurrent chemoradiation more convenient and potentially less toxic for patients treated in routine oncology practice.
method: Phase II, multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group superiority trial
300 patients randomized 1:1 to hypofractionated dose-painted VMAT vs conventional VMAT
Both arms receive weekly cisplatin and image-guided brachytherapy
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a prospective randomized design with clearly defined toxicity, survival, quality-of-life, and late-toxicity endpoints, but no outcome data are available yet.
watch_item: Because this is an unblinded, multicenter study with different fractionation and cisplatin doses, implementation and toxicity comparisons may be influenced by practice variability and the need for careful quality assurance.
paper_title: A phase II multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group, superiority study to compare the acute toxicity of Hypofractionated dOse Painted External radiotherapy versus conventional external radiotherapy in patients with carcinoma cervix stage I - IIB. (HOPE)
